## Working in this repo (sdlc)

This repo uses the sdlc workflow. It runs from the sdlc plugin in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity. Start or resume work through the plugin: its `start` command, or its `orchestrator` skill. If your agent doesn't have the plugin, follow these rules so that your work doesn't break the workflow's stage gates or its verification records.

- A feature's documents (intent, spec, plan) live in `docs/sdlc/intents/<feature>/`, and its state file lives under `.sdlc/state/`. Before changing code for a feature, read its spec and plan, and work only on the tasks the plan gives you.
- Never edit these files by hand. Only the sdlc workflow's own steps write them, because they record the stage gates and the verification evidence:
  - a feature's state file under `.sdlc/state/`
  - `.sdlc/baseline.md`, the list of failures that existed before
- If one of them needs to change, say so, and run the stage through the plugin, or ask a teammate who has the plugin to run it.
- A feature's state file names its `Owner:` (a git email) and `Tool:` (the agent). Before advancing a feature someone else owns, ask the user first: two people advancing one feature conflict on its state file. When the plugin advances it for a new owner, it records the handover.
- Use the project's commands exactly as written in `.sdlc/config.json`: `commands`, or for a monorepo, `commands` per package under `packages`. Run them from the package's directory. A full test run is the `test` command with no filters.
- The project's principles are in `docs/sdlc/constitution.md`. For team knowledge, open `knowledge/index.md` and follow its links as needed.
- Scratch files go in `.sdlc/.work/`, which git ignores.

## Project instructions (from CLAUDE.md)

### Heart UI

Open source Vue 3 UI library on Reka UI. Items (components, blocks, layouts,
themes) are source files copied into user projects by a CLI from a
shadcn-format registry. Package and CLI name: `heart-ui`.

#### Read before working

| File | Read when |
| --- | --- |
| [docs/spec.md](docs/spec.md) | Once, for product scope and goals |
| [docs/conventions.md](docs/conventions.md) | Before writing any code |
| [docs/tokens.md](docs/tokens.md) | Before styling anything |
| [docs/components/index.md](docs/components/index.md) | Before building a component |
| [docs/registry.md](docs/registry.md) | Before touching the CLI or registry build |
| [docs/layout-rules.md](docs/layout-rules.md) | Before building a block or layout |
| [docs/agent-support.md](docs/agent-support.md) | Before touching the MCP server, agent docs, or benchmark |
| [tasks/README.md](tasks/README.md) | To pick the next task |

#### Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm install` | Install the workspace |
| `pnpm check` | Full gate: lint, types, unit, browser, axe, visual, SSR, registry build, CLI end to end (needs the network) |
| `pnpm check:item <name>` | Same gate, scoped to one registry item |
| `pnpm dev:vite` / `pnpm dev:nuxt` | Run a playground |
| `pnpm registry:build` | Check the API snapshots, then emit registry JSON to `dist/registry` |
| `pnpm registry:api` | Regenerate each item's `<name>.api.json` after an API change |
| `pnpm test:visual --update` | Regenerate baselines. Human approval required. |

#### Working loop

1. Take the first task in `tasks/` whose status is `todo` and whose
   dependencies are `done`. One task per branch and pull request.
2. Read the task, then every doc it links.
3. Implement. Copy the structure of the reference components named in
   [docs/conventions.md](docs/conventions.md#reference-components).
4. Run the task's check command until it passes.
5. Set the task status to `review`, list what changed, and stop.

#### Hard rules

- Never mark a task `done`. A human does that after review.
- Never weaken a lint rule, test, or baseline to make a check pass.
- Never change a token value or name outside a task that says to.
- No raw values in `registry/`: no hex or named colors, no pixel or rem
  literals, no Tailwind palette or arbitrary-value classes.
- `reka-ui` imports only inside `registry/ui/`.
- User-facing text enters by prop or slot. The only literals allowed are
  English defaults of props named `*Label`.
- Do not add a dependency that the task or conventions do not name. Propose
  it in the pull request instead.
- Tasks with `owner: human` are not yours. Stop and report when one blocks you.
- When the docs conflict or leave a gap, add an entry to
  `docs/questions.md` and choose the option closest to the reference
  components. Do not guess silently.
- Check current upstream docs for Reka UI, Tailwind CSS v4, Nuxt 4, and the
  shadcn registry schema before using an API. Do not rely on memory.

## Area rules

### CI, build and infrastructure (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `.github/**`, `**/Dockerfile*`, `**/docker-compose*.{yml,yaml}`, `**/*.tf`, `{infra,infras,deploy,k8s,helm}/**`.

- Changes here need the user's go-ahead before they are committed: they affect everyone and every environment.
- Never weaken a required check (removing a step, adding `continue-on-error`, skipping tests or lint) to get green.
- CI runs the same commands as local work (`commands` in `.sdlc/config.json`). Change a command there, then let `/sdlc:upgrade` (Claude Code) regenerate the workflow, rather than editing CI steps so they drift from local runs.
- Pin actions and images to a version; never pass secrets through command-line arguments or logs.

### Code style (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs,cjs,vue,svelte}`, `**/*.{py,go,rs,java,kt,rb,php,cs,swift}`.

Comments
- Comment only the *why* the code can't show: a constraint, a non-obvious reason, a workaround with its cause.
- Never narrate or restate code ("Step 1", "Now we…", "This function…", "Loop over the items").
- Never reference the task, PR, ticket, conversation or change history ("added for X", "now uses Y", "fixed bug"). That belongs in git.
- Doc comments only on exported API, one line by default; add params/returns only when the contract isn't obvious from names and types.
- Match the comment density of the surrounding file.

Scope
- Write the smallest change that meets the acceptance criteria; edit existing code before adding new code.
- No abstraction with a single implementation, no options/params/config the spec didn't ask for, no handling of cases that can't happen.
- No new files, layers, dependencies or public exports the plan doesn't name. If you think one is needed, say so instead of adding it.
- Follow the patterns already in the codebase; don't restructure code outside the task.

### Schema migrations (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `**/migrations/**`, `**/migrate/**`, `**/db/migration/**`, `**/drizzle/**`, `**/alembic/**`, `**/prisma/schema.prisma`.

- Any migration is a hard stop: describe it and get the user's go-ahead before creating or running it.
- Never edit a migration that has been applied anywhere; add a new one.
- Every migration needs a tested rollback (down migration or written restore steps in the feature's `release.md`).
- Prefer additive, backward-compatible steps (add column → backfill → switch reads → drop later) over destructive ones.
- Why it matters: the deploy migrates before it moves traffic, so the running version meets the new schema first, and a rollback moves traffic back without undoing the migration, leaving the new schema under the old code. A migration must work with the app version before it.
- Work touching migrations is at least M track and always gets a security review after the build.

### Sensitive areas: auth, payments, secrets, PII (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `**/{auth,authn,authz,session,sessions}/**`, `**/*{secret,credential,crypto}*`, `**/.env*`, `.changeset/**`, `.npmrc`.

- Work here is at least M track and always gets a security review after the build.
- Never hardcode, log, print or commit secrets, tokens or PII; read secrets from the environment or the secret manager.
- Validate and authorize on the server for every request; never trust client-supplied identity, roles or amounts.
- Fail closed: on an error in an auth or payment check, deny.
- Don't change crypto, session or token handling without stating the threat it addresses.

### Tests (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `**/*.{test,spec}.*`, `**/{test,tests,__tests__,spec}/**`, `**/test_*.py`, `**/*_test.{py,go}`.

- Write the failing test first and watch it fail for the right reason (`sdlc:test-driven-development`).
- Assert observable behavior, not implementation details; one behavior per test, named after it.
- Never commit `.only`, `.skip`, `xit`, `@pytest.mark.skip` or a retried/flaky test to get green. Fix it or report it.
- Never weaken an assertion or delete a test to make it pass; that needs the user's explicit OK.
- Use real code over mocks where it's cheap; mock only at system boundaries (network, clock, randomness).
- Run the full suite with the `test` command from `.sdlc/config.json` before claiming anything passes; filtered runs don't count.

### UI (sdlc policy)

Applies when working on files matching `**/*.{tsx,jsx,vue,svelte,astro,html,css,scss,sass,less}`.

Design system
- Read `docs/sdlc/design-system.md` before UI work. It names the tokens, the component library and the patterns this project uses; follow it strictly.
- Colors, spacing, type, radius, shadows and motion come from tokens only: no raw hex/rgb, arbitrary Tailwind values (`w-[13px]`) or inline `style=`.
- Reuse the design system's components. A new component, variant or token needs a stated reason, and goes into the design system, not inline.
- No design system file yet? Say so and ask before building UI; don't invent one silently.

No AI slop
- No default "AI look": purple/blue gradients, glassmorphism, glow, blobs, oversized rounded cards, emoji as icons, gradient text, decorative shadows. Only what the design system defines.
- No generic filler: lorem ipsum, "Welcome to", "Get started today", three-feature-card heroes, stock testimonials. Use the spec's real copy or ask.
- Match the density, alignment and hierarchy of existing screens; don't restyle what the task didn't ask for.

Every screen
- Handle loading, empty, error and success states the spec names.
- Accessible by default: semantic elements, labels on inputs and icon buttons, visible focus, keyboard reachable, contrast from the system's tokens.

### App rules

Applies when working on files matching `apps/**/*`.

- Playgrounds import items from `registry/` by alias; never copy item code into an app. Node-side helpers (`apps/demo-*.ts`) may import registry types by relative path, since Node has no alias.
- Gallery routes are `/demo/<name>` with `theme`, `mode`, `dir` and (blocks, layouts) `state` query parameters — why: [phase-0 P0-04](../../tasks/phase-0.md)
- Visual baselines change only with `pnpm test:visual --update` and human approval.
- Docs site pages come from each item's `<name>.md` plus demo — why: [docs site](../../docs/conventions.md#docs-site)

### Package rules

Applies when working on files matching `packages/**/*`, `scripts/**/*`, `benchmark/**/*`.

- Write logic here test-first (constitution IV).
- Build Node packages with `tsdown`; pin dependency versions exactly — why: [toolchain](../../docs/conventions.md#toolchain)
- A change to a published package needs a changeset.
- CLI and registry build follow [registry.md](../../docs/registry.md); theme follows [tokens.md](../../docs/tokens.md).
- MCP server and benchmark follow [agent-support.md](../../docs/agent-support.md).

### Registry rules

Applies when working on files matching `registry/**/*`.

- Follow the item anatomy and API rules — why: [conventions](../../docs/conventions.md#item-anatomy)
- Style only with token utilities; no raw values, no `dark:` — why: [tokens](../../docs/tokens.md#lint-rule)
- Import `reka-ui` only under `registry/ui/`.
- Icons through `registry/lib/icon`, classes through `cn()` from `registry/lib/utils`.
- Copy the structure of `button`, `input`, `dialog` before inventing a pattern.
- Keep `item.json` valid against the shadcn schema; extra fields go under `meta` — why: [registry](../../docs/registry.md#item-metadata)
- Blocks and layouts obey every rule in [layout-rules.md](../../docs/layout-rules.md#rules).
- Check is `pnpm check:item <name>`.

Before building an item, check: [components/index.md](../../docs/components/index.md) and the Reka UI docs page for its primitive.
